title: Intelligence Brief
headline: Google shipped Gemini 4 Argon with a 1M-token output ceiling at $2/M input, $10/M output pricing
subtitle: Google shipped Gemini 4 Argon with a 1M-token, NVIDIA/OpenShell, the open-source Linux, OpenAI's DevDay shipped a Decisions API -- a

insights.text: Google shipped Gemini 4 Argon with a 1M-token output ceiling (up from 64K) at $2/M input, $10/M output pricing, replacing Gemini 3.5 Pro. It's rolling a version without cyber guardrails out only to vetted cyber-defense partners through its Fairwind Program plus internal teams, because Argon can locate, validate, and patch critical software vulnerabilities without human help -- gating general release specifically over that capability rather than cost or capacity.

NVIDIA/OpenShell, the open-source Linux Landlock/seccomp-BPF sandbox runtime for AI agents, jumped from GitHub Trending #2 (10,827 stars, 09-30) to #1 today (13,034 total, +1,281/day) -- a rank improvement rather than the usual second-day cooldown, the first trending-board evidence of sustained developer adoption beyond press coverage of its origin as NVIDIA's Open Agent Safety Platform sandbox component.

OpenAI's DevDay (Sept 29) shipped a Decisions API -- a constrained GPT-6 Luna router for classification, routing, and agent next-action decisions -- and extended the Agents API with Computer Use (an OpenAI-hosted browser agents can operate) plus a managed Codex harness where OpenAI handles sessions, orchestration, context compaction, and recovery. It's the first instance this vault has logged of a frontier lab offering the orchestration layer itself rather than leaving fleet management to third-party harnesses.

debpalash/VoiceStudio, the fully-local open-source ElevenLabs alternative, held a top-2 GitHub Trending slot for a third consecutive day (#2 today, 50,668 total stars) the same day TechCrunch reported ElevenLabs -- the closed, cloud-billed incumbent VoiceStudio brands itself against -- doubled its own valuation to $22B via a $300M employee tender led by existing backers Wellington and T. Rowe Price, not new capital. Read together: evidence for coexistence in different markets (self-hosted/no-cap vs. managed/enterprise) rather than open-source disruption already in progress.

mvschwarz/openrig, the YAML-defined Claude-Code-plus-Codex fleet harness, held GitHub Trending #3 today (3,141 total, up from #6/2,547 total yesterday) -- a net gain of roughly 594 stars confirming genuine second-day interest rather than debut-day noise in a tool that gives agent teams persistent, declaratively-specified tmux 'seats.'

Thursday's OTT/Streaming rotation found no new movement on either tracked merger: Fox-Roku's $22B deal remains under the DOJ's September 8 Second Request (waiting period extends 30 days past substantial compliance, H1 2027 close still expected per Roku's own SEC filings); Paramount/WBD's $111B merger stays resolved at its 09-24 antitrust settlement (behavioral film-release quota, no divestiture).

September 2026 shipped five Google Play platform release waves bringing a redesigned Contribution Hub (ratings/reviews with social-impact tracking), real-time Wallet-based cart price adjustments at checkout, and a new Apps Experience program alongside an updated Games Level Up program offering lower service-fee rate cards to compliant developers starting 2026-09-30 -- extending this vault's fee/trust-bifurcation thread from trust signals into fee structure itself.

heygen-com/hyperframes entered GitHub Trending (#10, 54,845 total) pitched as 'Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents' -- a new agent-targeted creative-CLI candidate rendering declarative markup to video rather than a timeline or script, alongside VoiceStudio's continued lead in the same category.
